U.S. General Services Administration Justification for other than full and open competition (1) Identification of the agency and the contracting activity: General Services Administration (GSA) Public Buildings Service (PBS) Acquisition Project Delivery Contracting Division - West (2) Nature and/or description of the action being approved: Furnish and installation of protest security barriers to provide forced entry protection of building occupants during protest events. (3) A description of the supplies or services required to meet the agency’s needs (including the estimated value): The services required include comprehensive site preparation and installation of temporary security barriers along the ██████████████████████████████████████ of the Eugene Federal Building. The contractor shall first complete site preparation work at 211 E 7th Ave, Eugene, OR, including removal of one (1) designated tree (approximately 25 feet tall with 30-inch diameter trunk), complete stump grinding to ground level, grading and leveling of a 5-foot by 60-foot sloped turf area, and application of 2-3 inches of medium fir bark. Following site preparation, the contractor shall supply and install an integrated barrier system (barriers must be gravity-based, not permanently affixed to the sidewalk) and relocate approximately ███ of fencing, concrete block style barriers and Jersey style barriers from a warehouse in ████. All work must comply with OSHA, National Electrical Code, and applicable safety standards, with proper handling of any hazardous materials per AHERA/OSHA/EPA requirements. The contractor must comply with GSA Building Security requirements, coordinate with city for right-of-way permits for sidewalk closures, maintain unobstructed emergency access, and ensure all personnel are properly escorted. The contractor shall provide detailed cost breakdowns by discrete work features, weekly progress updates, and a complete closeout package. The government estimated cost for this procurement is ███████ (4) An identification of the statutory authority permitting other than full and open competition: Unusual and compelling urgency - 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(2): Agencies may contract without providing for full and open competition when the agency’s need for the supplies or services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the Government would be seriously injured, financially or otherwise, unless the agency is permitted to limit the number of sources from which it solicits bids or proposals. (5) A demonstration that the proposed contractor’s unique qualifications or the nature of the acquisition requires use of the authority cited: This contractor has furnished and installed this specific type of anti-scaling protest barrier on federal courthouses throughout the country. Furthermore, they have direct experience installing the fencing on the ████ in recent years during major protest events. This is not standard fencing, it takes special hardware at the connections that also requires additional hardware to further secure the connections. Once those connections are complete, concrete barriers weighing several thousand lbs each are placed adjacent to the fencing to prevent the barrier from being toppled over during protest events. All of these construction activities need to be performed 100% complete during a very limited window of opportunity between protest events, something of which this contractor has very specific experience executing.

(6) A description of efforts made to ensure that offers are solicited from as many potential sources as is practicable, including whether a notice was or will be publicized as required by part 5 and, if not, which exception under part 5 applies: N/A, Using other than full and open competition (see 6.302-2) Unusual and compelling urgency. (7) A determination by the contracting officer that the anticipated cost to the Government will be fair and reasonable: GSA will establish that it is a fair and reasonable price by Comparison of the proposed prices to historical prices paid and Comparison of proposed prices with independent Government cost estimates. Historical pricing for similar work was recently executed at the █████████ ████████ (8) A description of the market research conducted (see part 10) and the results or a statement of the reason market research was not conducted: See market research report in file tab 6. (9) Any other facts supporting the use of other than full and open competition, such as: (i) When 6.302 (Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements) is cited for follow-on acquisitions as described in 6.302-1(2)(ii), an estimate of the cost to the Government that would be duplicated and how the estimate was derived. (ii) When 6.302-2(2)(unusual and compelling urgency) is cited, data, estimated cost, or other rationale as to the extent and nature of the harm to the Government. Due to ongoing protests, the Government faces an immediate emergency requiring urgent execution of these services. Without immediate action, there is an imminent and substantial risk of destruction to critical Government property, resulting in significant operational disruption and potential safety hazards. Any unnecessary delay caused by standard competitive procedures would unnecessarily risk severe harm to the Government's mission-critical operations and financial interests. The time-sensitive nature of this emergency necessitates limiting the number of sources to ensure rapid mobilization to prevent unnecessary risk to government property. (10) A listing of the sources, if any, that expressed, in writing, an interest in the acquisition: N/A (Sole Source) (11) A statement of the actions, if any, the agency may take to remove or overcome any barriers to competition before any subsequent acquisition for the supplies or services required: The Government will perform a technical analysis of the proposal, comparing proposed costs to historical pricing received for similar services and comparing to the Independent government estimate.

(12) Contracting officer certification that the justification is accurate and complete to the best of the contracting officer’s knowledge and belief:

Technical Personnel Justin Schoenberg Henry Huynh
